decision: The CHECK quotes each value by wrapping it in single quotes (f"'{p}'"); I did not use repr() or SQL escaping
why: repr() would emit double quotes for a value containing an apostrophe, and SQLite treats double quotes as an identifier. The allowed values are lowercase words, so plain single quotes are enough and the output stays character-for-character identical to the old string
result: T-01-check OK; before and after schema diff identical

decision: No new pytest test for "the values are in one place"; T-01-check.py is the driven check, and the unchanged parts are proven by breaking them and seeing the existing tests fail
why: A test that scans source for strings would pin the implementation. The ticket already names its check and the existing tests
result: check went from FAIL to OK; 75 passed

decision: The CHECK is built by string concatenation, not a nested f-string with the same quotes
why: Nesting f-strings with the same quotes only works on Python 3.12+, and the project does not state a minimum Python version

decision: Filter in the route, in Python, over store.list()/store.overdue(); store untouched

decision: priority is declared as list[str] so a repeat is seen; the repeat check runs before the value check (low&urgent says "only once")

decision: LIST_QUERY_VALUES["overdue"] lists what FastAPI's bool already accepted (true/false/1/0/yes/no/on/off/t/f/y/n, any letter case) instead of narrowing it

decision: The guard reads the list parameters from the app's OpenAPI schema. Its "value outside the table" probes are a sentinel, the empty string, and each declared value with a space before or after. It does not probe letter-case variants
why: A case-variant probe would fail on overdue, which accepts any letter case; priority's strict letter case is pinned by the S-3 tests instead
